project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
An innovative clean-tech solution brought to full technological maturity and close to market readiness along one specific value chain, in an industry-driven demonstration.
Proposals select one main area and may combine others: integrated net-zero energy systems (including energy grids, networks and systems); enhanced zero-emission power technologies; or storage, renewable fuels and carbon capture and utilisation. The applicants choose the value chain.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Proposals must address at least one of three clean-tech areas, with one main area, and meet four expectations.
Areas:
- integrated net-zero emissions energy systems, for example energy grids, networks and systems
- enhanced zero-emission power technologies, for example renewable electricity, heat and energy technologies
- storage technologies, renewable fuels and carbon capture and utilisation, for example batteries, renewable hydrogen, advanced biofuels and synthetic fuels
Expectations:
- develop innovative solutions along a specific value chain, with clean-tech suppliers, energy users (manufacturing, energy, transport) and other stakeholders, supporting a sound business case
- demonstrate integration of the solutions in support of the Clean Industrial Deal, directly (energy to an industrial or transport sector) or indirectly (energy to grid to an industrial or transport sector), with quantifiable impact on competitiveness and greenhouse-gas reduction
- show industrial leadership for deployment after the project, with an industry-driven consortium
- seek coherence with the SET Plan and industrial initiatives
Proposals may also address a step change in network and infrastructure deployment across trans-European energy and transport networks (electricity, heat, gas, hydrogen, CO2, batteries, refuelling). Technologies with negative impact on biodiversity should be avoided.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
EU industry must decarbonise competitively and Europe must manufacture clean technologies itself, which requires much more electrification and market-ready clean tech.
The need originates with industry and the EU economy: the Clean Industrial Deal aims to keep Europe attractive for manufacturing, including energy-intensive industry, while meeting climate and biodiversity targets, and the Net-Zero Industry Act sets goals for EU manufacturing capacity of net-zero technologies.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A demonstrated clean-tech solution close to market, plus engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, permits, a business plan and a market-readiness strategy.
- Before the go/no-go moment: detailed engineering plans, a techno-economic assessment, all permits for the demonstrator, a complete business plan and market-readiness strategy, and the industrial partners that will lead deployment
- The demonstrator, after a go decision
- Yearly updates of the business plan and market-readiness strategy as deliverables, and a final report
- An analysis of technological and non-technological barriers to deployment, with a plan to address them
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 28–29 · Horizontal call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal, Instructions for the Business Plan and the Market-Readiness Strategy

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to both outcomes: a more competitive, sustainable and resilient clean-tech solution, and its maturity close to market readiness.
- Significantly strengthen competitiveness, sustainability (including biodiversity) and resilience of the solution, by increasing its circular material use rate and reducing the levelised cost of energy (average cost per unit of energy delivered) to end users, each against a realistic baseline, and by contributing to EU industrial leadership in line with the Net-Zero Industry Act
- Bring the solution to full technological maturity and close to market readiness, accelerating deployment or integration in key industrial sectors such as manufacturing, energy and transport
- Supply-chain rule: for each main component where more than 50% of EU supply comes from a third country, at least 50% should be sourced from the EU or Associated Countries, unless justified
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The project must end fit for deployment, with industrial partners named to lead it and a business plan aimed at further private or public investment.
- A business plan and market-readiness strategy, backed by company management, decisive under the impact criterion and updated yearly
- The market-readiness strategy must cover obstacles such as investment, regulation, permitting, standards, skills, product robustness, industrial integrators, IP and user acceptance, with a full risk assessment
- Deployment across EU industrial sectors or through further investment, including EU programmes such as the Innovation Fund
- The granting authority may object, for up to 4 years after the project, to a transfer of ownership or exclusive licensing of results
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 28–29 · Horizontal call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal, Instructions for the Business Plan and the Market-Readiness Strategy

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
The consortium should be manageable: indicatively not more than ten participants, with its size justified by the extent of the value chain covered.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The consortium should be industry-driven and combine clean-tech suppliers, energy users and other stakeholders along one value chain; SME participation is encouraged.
Energy users named are manufacturing, energy and transport. A gender-sensitive and intersectional approach should be taken into account. Entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The work is split by a go/no-go moment: preparation (engineering, assessment, permits, business plan) first, then contracting and demonstration.
The industrial partners that will lead deployment must be clearly identified before the go/no-go moment. The call sets no budget split among partners.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
Since the consortium should be industry-driven, an industrial partner is the natural lead; this is our reading, not a rule.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Possible but unlikely: the consortium should be industry-driven, and TenneT TSO B.V. would more naturally be the grid partner in an energy-systems value chain.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible. TenneT must not be controlled by China or a Chinese entity.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
With a guideline of at most ten participants, TenneT may be more welcome as an associated partner if its role is advisory.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary TenneT can receive up to 70% of its eligible costs; it must fund the rest itself.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market), for which the maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities. The grant reimburses costs actually incurred plus a 25% flat rate for indirect costs. The expected EU contribution is EUR 15–25 million per project, for the whole consortium. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
In the integrated energy systems area, TenneT could be the grid partner in an energy-to-grid-to-industry value chain, for example for electrified industry.
This is our interpretation. The call allows indirect integration via the grid and a step change in network deployment, which matches TenneT's Target Grid 2045 and its Grid Investment Plans for industrial clusters. TenneT could provide connection design, flexible access arrangements and system studies. The solution itself must be a clean-tech product brought to market by industry, so TenneT would support rather than own the innovation.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The solution must be innovative and reach full technological maturity close to market readiness; earlier EU or national R&I results may be used.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Mainly technology and its industrial integration, combined with business models and market-readiness arrangements along a value chain.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 28–29 · Horizontal call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal, Instructions for the Business Plan and the Market-Readiness Strategy

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Engineering, permitting and planning up to a go/no-go moment, then demonstration and preparation for deployment.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to start at TRL 6 and reach TRL 8 by the end of the project.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 8 is a complete and qualified system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: A demonstrator is required after the go/no-go moment, for which all permits must be in place beforehand; integration into industry or transport must be shown.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Clean-tech and industrial decarbonisation solutions must be integrated directly into an industrial or transport sector, or indirectly via the grid.
Projects are encouraged to coordinate with projects under the Clean Industrial Deal topics on energy-intensive industries and with partnerships such as the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking and the Clean Energy Transition Partnership.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: The project must show quantifiable impact on competitiveness and greenhouse-gas reduction, and improvements in circular material use and cost of energy against realistic baselines.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: Energy users from manufacturing, energy and transport must be part of the value-chain consortium.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
The call sets no cybersecurity requirement; it excludes Chinese-controlled entities and requires a risk assessment in the market-readiness strategy.
- Control restriction: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
- Risk: a comprehensive risk assessment is mandatory in the market-readiness strategy
- Satellite data: if used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 28–29 · Horizontal call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal, Instructions for the Business Plan and the Market-Readiness Strategy

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 8 projects of EUR 15–25 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 140 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: EUR 15–25 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 7–8 · Call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal (HORIZON-CID-2027-01), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium roles

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 15 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 15 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 60 pages, extended to include the business plan and market-readiness strategy; the main area must be selected
- Opening: 12 January 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 7–8 · Call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal (HORIZON-CID-2027-01), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions, Admissibility conditions and Procedure

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around February 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 60 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Business plan and market-readiness strategy: mandatory for all proposals, backed by company management
- Go/no-go: the proposal must include a go/no-go moment and a credible pathway to all permits
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 28–29 · Horizontal call R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal, Instructions for the Business Plan and the Market-Readiness Strategy

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
- Portfolio rule: besides ranking order, at least the highest-ranked proposal for each of the three areas is funded, according to the main area selected, if it passes all thresholds
- Impact: the business plan and market-readiness strategy are decisive factors under the Impact criterion
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
A 60-page limit, a mandatory business plan, a go/no-go moment, a supply-chain sourcing rule and an area portfolio rule are specific to this topic.
- Exception — page limit: 60 pages for Part B
- Conditional — go/no-go: engineering plans, techno-economic assessment, permits, business plan and deployment lead identified before the demonstration
- Conditional — sourcing: at least 50% of main components that the EU mostly imports should come from the EU or Associated Countries, unless justified
- Exception — ranking: the top proposal per area is funded if it passes the thresholds
- Exception — entities controlled by China: not eligible
- Conditional — results transfer: the granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licensing for 4 years after the project
- Recommended: at most about ten participants; SME participation; coordination with related Clean Industrial Deal projects
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · HORIZON-CID-2027-01-02, Specific conditions and Expected Outcome and Scope
